record.paper_title: Recent Theoretical Advances and Open Problems in Nuclear Cluster Physics
record.context_brief: Ab initio validation of the Hoyle state
record.original_question: Can ab initio descriptions of the carbon-12 Hoyle state, especially no-core Monte Carlo shell-model, symmetry-adapted no-core shell-model, and lattice QMC-EFT approaches, be validated by reproducing the Hoyle-state inelastic form factor, transition probabilities, and radius, rather than reproducing only parts of the spectrum or energy position?

evidence.quote: So far no inelastic form factor has been calculated but the monopole t ransition probability comes out quite reasonable. Also the position is reasonably accurate. However, to be totally con vinced of the approach the inelastic form factor is needed.
However, no transition probability or inelasti c form factor have been calculated. As said above, without tho se ingredients, it is di ﬃcult to judge the value of the approach.

On the other hand neither in elastic form factor nor the transition probability have been attempted to be calculated. Even the radius, see below, completely fails since it is barely larger than the one of the ground state.
This concerns for instance the reproduction of the inelastic form factor of the Hoyle state what we think is absolutely necessary to give a ﬁnal credit to a correct theor y for the Hoyle state.

artifact.status_search_result: Lattice EFT and other ab initio methods have reproduced the Hoyle state energy and monopole transition matrix element, and recent work (e.g., 2024–2025 lattice EFT and no-core shell-model studies) has begun to compute electromagnetic form factors and radii for light nuclei. However, a fully consistent ab initio reproduction of the Hoyle inelastic form factor F(q), the monopole transition probability, and the enlarged Hoyle radius simultaneously across all listed frameworks has not yet been definitively achieved; the question remains an active validation challenge.

status_evidence.title: Ab initio calculation of the Hoyle state
status_evidence.snippet: First ab initio lattice-EFT calculation finding a resonance with Hoyle-state properties at the correct energy.
status_evidence.claim: Energy and basic structure of the Hoyle state were obtained ab initio, but form-factor validation was not yet provided.

status_evidence.title: The Hoyle state in Nuclear Lattice EFT
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews NLEFT results for the Hoyle state spectrum and electromagnetic properties.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent NLEFT work addresses electromagnetic properties but full inelastic form-factor reproduction is still under development.

status_evidence.title: Alpha-Particle Monopole Form Factors with Ab Initio No-Core Shell Model
status_evidence.snippet: Recent ab initio computation of monopole form factors in light nuclei.
status_evidence.claim: Ab initio form-factor calculations are progressing but a complete validation for the ¹²C Hoyle state is ongoing.

status_evidence.title: Lattice Effective Field Theory Simulations of Nuclei (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews recent NLEFT progress on ¹²C and ¹⁶O including electromagnetic observables.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates partial progress on form factors and radii within ab initio frameworks.
